profile.regional_context: Per Google's own data center location page, Google established the Council Bluffs facility in 2007 with an initial $600 million investment and has invested over $20 billion in Iowa since. A $7 billion expansion was announced to grow the Council Bluffs campus and establish a new Cedar Rapids, Iowa data center. Google also cites a NextEra Energy agreement tied to restarting Iowa's Duane Arnold nuclear plant as part of its regional power strategy, and $1.3 million toward a 47-site water quality/grade stabilization project.

reading.body:
Google operates a multi-building data center campus in Council Bluffs, Pottawattamie County, Iowa, established in 2007 as part of a $20 billion investment across the state. The company does not publish power capacity, square footage, or individual building addresses for this campus, disclosing only aggregate state-level investment figures. This disclosure policy places the campus outside the set of facilities where published megawatt capacity can be verified.

Among Iowa's 52 mapped data center facilities, only two operators publish power specifications to this registry, totaling 18 MW of disclosed capacity across the state. This campus ranks third by published megawatt figures in Iowa, though the campus's own power draw remains undisclosed and cannot be compared directly to other sites.

Google's stated regional power strategy ties to a NextEra Energy agreement to restart the Duane Arnold nuclear plant to support the Council Bluffs campus expansion, indicating substantial unannounced capacity growth. Without published megawatt figures, the campus cannot be sized against other AI infrastructure, but the scale of Google's capital commitment in Iowa and the nuclear power arrangement suggest the campus is material to regional grid planning even if its exact capacity remains private.
